questions.question: What does Spring Boot mainly add on top of the Spring Framework?
options: A new programming language that replaces Java
Starters, auto-configuration and an embedded server
A frontend library for building web pages
questions.explanation: Spring Boot keeps Java and Spring, and adds starters, auto-configuration and an embedded server so apps start with little setup.

questions.question: With spring-boot-starter-webmvc and no extra settings, which port does the embedded Tomcat server listen on?
questions.explanation: The default port is 8080, and you can change it with server.port in application.properties.

questions.question: A @RestController has record Item(String name, int price) {} and the method @GetMapping("/items") List<Item> items() { return List.of(new Item("Pen", 20)); }. What does GET /items return?
questions.explanation: Inside a @RestController, Jackson turns the returned list of records into a JSON array.

questions.question: The @SpringBootApplication class is in com.shop.app and a @RestController is in com.shop.web. The app starts, but GET /products returns 404. What is the bug?
options: The controller method must be static
Port 8080 is blocked by the browser
The controller is outside the package that component scan covers
questions.explanation: @SpringBootApplication scans its own package and the packages below it, and com.shop.web is not under com.shop.app.

questions.question: A student pastes import javax.persistence.Entity; from an old blog post into a Spring Boot 4 project. What happens?
options: It compiles, because Spring Boot 4 accepts both packages
It fails to compile, because Spring Boot 4 uses jakarta.persistence
Spring Boot rewrites the import automatically at startup
It works, but only on Java 8
questions.explanation: Since Spring Boot 3, Spring uses Jakarta EE, so the class now lives in jakarta.persistence and the javax import cannot be found.
